entries.title: delete the Release PR's runs that wait for approval
entries.body:
The Release PR's push and title edit, made with the default
GITHUB_TOKEN, raise CI and PR title `pull_request` runs that wait as
`action_required`. GitHub's merge box refuses to merge while any run at
the head waits for approval, even one no ruleset requires, so the
Release PR could not merge until a maintainer approved runs that only
repeat what the dispatched runs already checked. release-pr.yml now
deletes those waiting runs for a minute after it pushes; a run it
cannot delete is named in a warning.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: report the dispatched CI gate as a ci-gate commit status
entries.body:
* ci: report the dispatched CI gate as a ci-gate commit status

A pull request's required checks count only check runs from push,
pull_request and a few other events, never from workflow_dispatch, so
the Release PR's dispatched CI left the ruleset's required ci-gate
"Waiting for status to be reported" even though the gate passed on the
PR's head. A commit status counts whatever made it, so on a dispatched
run ci.yml's gate now also posts its outcome as a ci-gate status on the
commit it tested, with statuses: write on that job alone.

Refs: docs/wp12-release.md

* test: retire the fuzz declaration 0.44.0 shipped

The 0.44.0 seed carries the loop-guarded additions, so fuzz.js's
declaration for them covered no program and failed as stale in both
nish-cmp lanes. onlyAddsLoopGuards stays, held to its fabricated pairs.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: record the cookbook regen check and nish-cmp --no-sidecars for wasm32 in CLAUDE.md
entries.body:
Two conventions the WP48 stage 6 run (#1740) found unwritten: docs/IR_COOKBOOK.md
is generated by docs/cookbook/regen.sh and checked after the suite in CI's
shard 1, and a default nish-cmp run reports a wasm32 program whose sidecar
build both compilers refuse as refused by both rather than as a difference.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: plan WP74 to WP79, the std and toolchain gaps a generated API CLI meets
entries.body:
* docs: plan WP74 to WP79, the std and toolchain gaps a generated API CLI meets

Six plans for what a Nish command-line API client needs and the library or
toolchain lacks: form and multipart bodies, server-sent events and decoded
responses (WP74); client certificates, macOS Keychain roots and an opt-in
TLS 1.2 profile (WP75); an HTTP/2 client (WP76); a credential store (WP77);
linking for another target (WP78); and Windows as a target (WP79).

* docs: record the issue numbers of WP74 to WP79
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: check a record's cited checks and figures against their source before the PR
entries.body:
Three of four review rounds on #1707 (WP48 stage 1) were spent on record
text that said more than the code: check(...) names that did not exist,
a 15 GiB cap claimed for the whole arena, and budget rows that disagreed
with their constants. CLAUDE.md already says a record states only what its
code does; this names the mechanical check that enforces it.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: name break-web's build as a --help input, and refresh apt before the compiler-rt install
entries.body:
* chore: name break-web's build as a --help input, and refresh apt before the compiler-rt install

CLAUDE.md now says that a change to --help or scripts/build.sh regenerates
examples/break-web's committed build in the same commit. Both PRs of the
link-pgo run (#1764, #1783) spent CI cycles on a stale break-web build.

The SessionStart hook installed libclang-rt-18-dev without refreshing the
package index, which fails in a fresh image whose LLVM tools are already
present. That left the instrumented PGO link without its profile runtime.

Refs: #1761

* docs: fold the break-web rule into the existing --help sentence

Main already states that a --help change regenerates break-web's files;
extend that sentence with scripts/build.sh, merges of main and the
regenerate-on-conflict rule instead of repeating it in a second paragraph.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make std/ panic-free for strict modules
entries.body:
std/collections, std/text, std/json, std/array, std/regex, std/sort, std/threads and std/net no longer reach a panic site from a strict module: indexes are guarded or proven, and real failures return a Result (nish/bytes gains tryCopyBytes). Examples and guide snippets that only opted out with --allow-panics because of std/ calls now build strict, and their opt-outs are gone.

Every smoked example pins its stdout; nish run, --emit-ts and --compat are tested without the flag; and a check fails on a stale opt-out, a flagged fence or example that builds strict.

Fixes #2065
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: pin vector 0.6.0 and regenerate the spec tests
entries.body: The spec tests are now emitted by vector 0.6.0. The eight contracts re-extract unchanged; the hex and RFC 8439 tests take vector's new byte-order integer helper in place of le64. contracts/README.md describes the forms 0.6.0 adds (command sources that print an integer, bool or null, window and out-buffer parameters, byte-order integer operations, Secret parameters in a property, values placed by RFC case headings and wrapped labels), and rfcs/ gains RFC 6234 and RFC 6979 for the SHA-2 and P-256 ECDSA specs to come.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: cover the HMAC and HKDF Secret exports in their RFC contracts
entries.body: vector 0.6.0 accepts Secret<u8[]> in a ts-interface block, so the RFC 4231 and RFC 5869 contracts now test hmacSha{256,384,512}Secret and the six HKDF *Secret exports through properties against their plain twins. hkdfExtractSha384 and hkdfExpandSha384 move into scope as those twins, held to RFC 5869 §2.2/§2.3 with HashLen 48. The keyed and scratch-class *Into exports stay out of scope, each quoting vector 0.6.0's refusal of a class parameter.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: state the PBKDF2 and SCRAM laws and record why their vectors keep commands
entries.body: Adds law sections to the RFC 7914 PBKDF2 and SCRAM-SHA-256 specs (prefix, refusal, Hi, proof and server-signature laws) and a requirement pinning PBKDF2's refusal of a count or length below 1, which spec mutate showed was unpinned. Each row records why vector 0.6.0 cannot cite its RFC value: the label grammar refuses RFC 7914's parenthesised labels, RFC 7677 prints its values only as base64, and integer labels repeat across rows.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: record why the RFC 8439 quarter-round positions stay uncited
entries.body: Every RFC 8439 vector #1671 listed as omitted is already a row of the rfc8439 contract. The spec now says why the quarter-round word positions stay uncited: Section 2.1.1 prints none, and Section 2.2.1's "2, 7, 8, 13" needs a label grammar vector 0.6.0 does not have. The THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md row for the spec now describes what Nish added to vector's copy.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: specify base64 and base64url from RFC 4648
entries.body: A spec-first vector contract for nish/crypto/base64url and nish/base64, cited from RFC 4648. The section 10 vectors drive the standard encoder, its buffer form and the decoder. Properties hold the URL codec equal to the standard one with the alphabet swapped and the padding dropped, along with round trips, lengths, canonical decoding and refusals. nish/base64 is held equal to the strict encoder. Base 32 and base 16, line-feed decoding, and decoder input above U+007F (vector 0.6.0 alphabets are printable ASCII) are recorded as out of scope.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: specify P-256 ECDSA signing from RFC 6979
entries.body: Adds a spec-first vector contract for std/crypto/p256.ts's sign, verify and public-key functions, cited from RFC 6979. The two A.2.5 SHA-256 vectors ("sample" and "test") match RFC 6979 byte for byte, and sampled properties pin the key range, signature form, round trip and tamper rejection. The verify rows, the public-key vector and the non-SHA-256 rows are left out because vector 0.6.0 cannot state them; the spec records each reason.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: add nish/net/protobuf, protobuf's wire format, with its security record
entries.body:
nish/net/protobuf reads and writes protobuf's wire format without a schema, the encoding gRPC carries its messages in. ProtoReader walks a message's fields in a u8[] span, skips unknown fields by wire type, and turns every malformed message into a sticky negative PROTO_ERR_* code instead of a panic; nesting is capped at PROTO_MAX_DEPTH (100) without recursion. ProtoWriter appends fields to a caller's buffer, backpatches embedded-message lengths, refuses bad field numbers, unbalanced nesting and messages past PROTO_MAX_SIZE, and allocates nothing once warm. Every index is guarded, so programs under the default no-panic check can call it. The module lands with its security record, docs/security/protobuf.md.

Tests: tests/link/net_protobuf, tests/link/net_protobuf_f64, tests/link/net_protobuf_bad_*
Fixes #2009
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: specify SHA-1 and SHA-2 from RFC 6234
entries.body: Adds spec-first vector contracts for std/crypto's sha1, sha256, sha384 and sha512, one per module (rfc6234-sha1, rfc6234-sha256, rfc6234-sha512), cited from RFC 6234. Each pins §8.5 tests 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 plus digest-length properties; sha384 is also checked against a truncated sha512. Expected digests come from python3 hashlib, checked against the RFC's printed hex, because vector cannot read §8.5's C-literal tables. The million-"a" test, the extra-bits tests and the streaming classes are left out because vector 0.6.0 cannot state them; each spec records the reason.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: trailers on the nish/net/http-server façade's HTTP/2 answers
entries.body:
A handler behind the nish/net/http-server façade can now end an HTTP/2 answer with trailers, the trailing header block gRPC carries its status in. Trailers are sent only on HTTP/2; asking for them on an HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/3 answer, after the body has ended, before the answer has started, or with malformed fields fails the program with a fixed exit code and message instead of sending a broken frame. The http-server security record and the user-guide page describe the new call.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_carriers, tests/link/net_http_server_trailers_*
Fixes #2013
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: read emit-ts strings without re-encoding them per byte
entries.body: An --emit-ts program's string reads found a string's UTF-8 bytes through a cache of one string, so std loops that alternate two strings (indexOfAnyFrom, yamlByte) re-encoded the whole document on every byte. The runtime now keeps the last 8 strings it read, most recent first. It never encodes an ASCII string and answers ASCII reads with the engine's own string methods. A 100 KB YAML load under Node 22 goes from about 1.2 s to about 25 ms, and a 3 MB one that did not finish in 120 s now loads in about 1 s.
metrics: yaml 100KB 1217 ms -> 24.2-27.0 ms per document (4.9x-5.4x of wasm), json 3MB 313 -> 256-363 ms; bands and runs in the PR
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: add nish/net/grpc, unary gRPC calls on the HTTP/2 listeners, with its security record (WP72 S3)
entries.body:
Programs can now answer unary gRPC calls on nish/net/http-server's HTTP/2 listeners (listenHttp2Tls, listenH2c) with nish/net/grpc. A call is an ordinary router route; GrpcServer.call checks the request and answers every fault itself (505 off HTTP/2, 415 for a wrong content-type, INTERNAL for a malformed grpc-timeout or bad framing, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED for a compressed message, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED past maxMessage) before the program sees it. reply sends the length-prefixed message with grpc-status 0 in the trailers; fail sends a status with a percent-encoded grpc-message, or the Trailers-Only form. Deadlines are capped at GrpcLimits.maxTimeout and checked at each call rather than by a timer. Streaming and compression are out of scope. The module ships with its security record (docs/security/grpc.md) and a user-guide page.

Tests: tests/link/net_grpc
Fixes #2014
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: call the gRPC server with pinned grpcurl and ghz over TLS and h2c (WP72 S4)
entries.body:
The interop workflow now checks nish/net/grpc against stock gRPC clients. A new grpc job starts a Nish gRPC server (tests/link/net_grpc_interop/serve.ts, built into the interop image) and calls it over TLS and h2c with grpcurl 1.9.3 and ghz 0.120.0. Each tool is fetched by pinned release and checked by SHA-256 before it runs. Per listener, the job checks two sums, a PermissionDenied with a percent-decoded message, a Trailers-Only NotFound, and DeadlineExceeded from the server's 1 s cap. It also runs 2000 ghz calls, 10 at a time, with jq checking that every one is OK. A ci-scope check fails when the job reads a file its pull_request paths do not cover.

Tests: tests/link/net_grpc_interop, tests/interop/grpc/check.sh
Refs: docs/security/grpc.md, docs/wp72-grpc.md

Fixes #2016
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: lend(x) reads a spawner's object in place (design B)
entries.body:
lend(x) from nish:async lets a spawned task read its spawner's object in place, with no copy into the task's region; it lowers to its argument. A lent view keeps its spawner's origin: storing into it, growing it, keeping it past the task, returning it, or storing it into the task's own fields or arrays is refused with NL2822, and lend of a number with NL2693. An array or object literal holding a lent view is itself lent. nish/net/serve now reads each request in place (ServeConns.lendOut / giveBack), and Http1Connection.lendParsed keeps a lent head out of the head pool until it is given back.

The TechEmpower gate was re-run with bench/techempower/run.sh unchanged and is not met: 7 of 11 judged cells are inside the band (before: 5 inside, 5 outside, 1 not judgeable). async's Ir/req fell by 316 on /plaintext and 286 on /json. The record is in docs/BENCHMARKS.md and docs/wp49-async-server.md section 10.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: inline integer conversions under --emit-ts
entries.body:
`--emit-ts` now writes integer width conversions at the call site instead of calling the runtime's `convert`. Examples are `| 0`, `>>> 0`, the byte and halfword masks, `BigInt.asIntN` and `BigInt.asUintN`, and a clamp around `| 0` for f64 to i32. `convert` is left as it was: growing it cost V8 its inlining in #2108. An ASCII `substring` with a NaN index now returns "", as native does.

Measured: emit-ts/wasm, YAML 100 KB 5.1x -> 4.2x (+-12.3%), JSON 100 KB 6.4x -> 2.5x, 5 rounds of bench/emit-ts-strings; ct_asm_x25519 under --emit-ts 10.2-11.8 s -> 7.9-9.1 s over 6 runs
Tests: tests/emit-ts/numbers/widths, tests/emit-ts/encodes/cache.mjs
Fixes #2120
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: answer Accept-Encoding: deflate with a zlib body
entries.body:
nish/net/http-compress now answers Accept-Encoding: deflate with a zlib-framed body (RFC 1950, which RFC 9110 means by deflate), alongside gzip. Before this, deflate was negotiated but never produced, so a client that accepted only deflate got identity.

A deflate body is written by the same gzip encoders and reframed in place: the gzip header becomes the 2-byte zlib header and an Adler-32 replaces the CRC-32 and length, 12 bytes shorter. respondEncoded's identity-refused forcing stays gzip-only; docs/security/compress.md records that scope (COMP-15) and accepts deflate with identity;q=0 going out as identity (COMP-17).

Refs: docs/guide (compression, "Deflate as well as gzip")
Tests: tests/link/std_http_compress

Fixes #1906
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: a mulHigh builtin for the 64×64→128 high product
entries.body:
* feat(checker): a mulHigh builtin for the 64×64→128 high product

`mulHigh(a, b)` returns the high 64 bits of the 128-bit product of two
`u64`s, and `mulHighIsNative()` says whether the target computes it in
one instruction. On 64-bit targets it lowers to an i128 multiply and
shift; on wasm32 to four 32×32 products with no i128 and no libcall.
Under --emit-ts both read from nish/runtime.

Refs: docs/wp41-mul-high.md

* test(checker): pin mulHigh's product, lowerings and refusal

A 10^6-pair sweep against the four-product reference, single-instruction
pins for x86-64 (mulq) and AArch64 (umulh), a wasm32 lowering with no i128
or __multi3, the NL2805 refusal, and the emit-ts reading.

Tests: tests/cases/mul_high_basic, tests/link/mul_high_reject_operand

* perf(codegen): P-256 and the JSON tokenizer take their high products from mulHigh

p256FiatMulxU64Hi and jsonTokMulHigh built a 64x64 high product from four
32x32 products. Both are gone: their callers call the mulHigh builtin, one
mul or umulh on x86-64 and AArch64. tests/run.js now holds mulHigh's machine
code to the ct-asm checker with both operands secret, on x86-64 and aarch64.
The language rule, the cookbook entry, the guide section, the security
records and the reference pages land with it.

Measured: p256 verify 1.330x min, 1.347x median; sign 1.357x min, 1.249x median (native, 11 interleaved rounds; base against its byte-identical copy 0.987x-1.036x verify, 1.010x-1.052x sign). wasm32 p256 assembly is byte-identical to base. JSON tokenize, canada.json, 1.01x min, 0.97x median, inside its 2.3%-4.5% bands; twitter, citm, typed and body inside their bands
Refs: docs/BENCHMARKS.md#the-mulhigh-builtin-in-p-256-and-the-json-tokenizer-wp41-s1
Tests: tests/link/crypto_p256_inverse, tests/cases/mul_high_native

* test(self): declare mulHigh's nish-cmp differences and regenerate the goldens

The seed refuses mulHigh, so the programs that call it compile only under
the candidate, and nish/json-tokenizer's IR moves with jsonTokMulHigh gone.

Tests: tests/nish-cmp.js

* fix(checker): check mulHigh's operands without a loop

The loop that checked each operand kept the error's type name on every
pass, a new NL9011 performance warning in src/. A helper called once per
operand checks the same thing.

Tests: tests/link/mul_high_reject_operand

* test(self): regenerate the builtins golden for the mulHigh operand check

Tests: tests/self/goldens/checked/src/builtins.ts.txt

* test(checker): pin each mulHigh refusal and its wasm32 lowering in std

Each operand refusal (u32, i64, an untyped `number`) and the arity refusal
is its own tests/link negative, and the emit-ts fixture calls mulHigh on
literal operands, which the call types u64. tests/run.js now holds the
wasm32 builds of std/crypto/p256.ts and std/json-tokenizer.ts to no i128 in
the IR and no __multi3 in the machine code that calls mulHigh. The
tokenizer's checked i64 multiply elsewhere is a __multi3 call on wasm32, so
only its jsonTokEiselLemire is held to that.

The records say what was run: the wasm32 P-256 assembly is identical to
the base's (the command and its sha256 are in docs/BENCHMARKS.md), the
twitter.json minimum is stated as past its bands, ECC-9 quotes its P-256
figures, and docs/crypto-performance.md no longer calls the 64×64→128
product missing. runtime/core.d.ts imports u64 for mulHigh on its own line.

Measured: wasm32 p256.s sha256 1cadc922 at 9996c9b1 and 88d046fc, identical
Refs: docs/LANGUAGE.md#mulhigh
Tests: tests/link/mul_high_reject_signed, tests/link/mul_high_reject_number, tests/link/mul_high_reject_arity, tests/emit-ts/numbers/mulhigh

* fix(checker): number mulHigh's operand refusal NL2819, after main's c-import codes

* docs(checker): regenerate the reference for mulHigh's NL2819 after main's merge

The merge of main took main's generated diagnostics pages; regenerating them
adds NL2819, mulHigh's operand refusal, beside main's c-import NL2805..NL2818.

Measured: no runtime change
Refs: docs/reference/diagnostics/nl2xxx.md
Tests: tests/link/mul_high_reject_operand

* docs: point WP41's design note at its issue now that main retired docs/roadmap

* test: build the mulHigh checks through spawnNish, now that main holds fixtures to no panic by default

* test: regenerate the mulhigh emit-ts golden for inlined integer conversions

Main's #2121 writes integer width conversions inline under --emit-ts instead of calling the runtime's convert, so the mulhigh golden's u64 literals change.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: WP43 S5 — middleware, steps that run before and after route bodies
entries.body:
A program can now register steps, work many routes share such as a token
check or a request-id field, that run before and after a route body on every
HTTP version. Router.step names one and Router.use binds it to a route (or to
the not-found and method-not-allowed answers); HttpHandler and HttpServer gain
before, after and field. A step may refuse the request with its own answer,
which stops the route body and every later step, or add answer fields, which
pass through each carrier's field checks.

Steps are pulled by the program's loop: a loop that never calls before and
after pays nothing per request, and one that does pays about 26 instructions a
request for the pair on a route bound to no step.

Fixed in review: a step that added content-length or alt-svc no longer sends
the field twice (HTTPSRV-16).

Measured: 25.0 to 26.8 Ir/request for HttpHandler's before+after pair on a route bound to no step (cachegrind, 3 interleaved rounds)
Refs: docs/wp43-http-app-layer.md, docs/BENCHMARKS.md
Tests: tests/link/net_handler_steps, tests/link/net_http_server_steps, tests/link/net_router

Fixes #2007
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: nish proto writes message classes from a .proto file (WP72 S5)
entries.body:
`nish proto <file.proto> -o <out.ts> [--check]` reads a proto3 file and writes one deterministic Nish module: a class per message with `encode` onto `ProtoWriter` and `decode` from `ProtoReader`, an `i32` constant per enum value, and a `string` constant per service method holding its gRPC path. `--check` keeps a checked-in module in step with its `.proto` file in CI. Exit codes: 0 written or current, 1 refused or stale, 2 usage.

The subset is proto3 scalars, nested messages and enums, `repeated` (written packed, read either way), `optional` with a `has_<field>` flag, `map<K, V>` with integer, bool or string keys, `oneof` with `<oneof>_case`, and unary services. Anything else (proto2, `import`, `stream`, unknown options, bad numbers or names, clashes in the generated module) is refused with the construct and its line, and nothing is written. Generated decoders keep the reader's limits and compile under the default panic rule; the protobuf security record gains PB-6 for their linear growth.

Fixes #2017
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: serve static files with MIME types, ETag, Range and traversal refused
entries.body:
nish/net/static serves a directory through the HTTP handler. The Content-Type comes from the file's extension, and every answer carries an ETag and a Last-Modified. A conditional request gets 304, a satisfiable Range gets 206 with exactly those bytes, and an unsatisfiable one gets 416. A precompressed .br or .gz sibling is served when the client accepts it. A path that leaves the root, encoded or not, is refused, and a file changed on disk is served changed with no restart. examples/http-app serves a directory through the module, and docs/security/static.md records its scope.

Part of #2123
Fixes #485
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: streaming request bodies on the façade's HTTP/2 listeners (WP72 S6a)
entries.body:
A route marked with HttpServer.streamBody is handed over at HEADERS on the HTTP/2 listeners (TLS and h2c). Its body arrives as DATA pieces the program reads from r.body[0 .. r.bodyLength) and hands back with HttpServer.consume. The stream's receive window is credited only as the program consumes, so a streamed request never holds more than one stream window of unread body, whatever maxBody is. The request comes out of take again for each piece, for the end, and for a reset or a lost connection. Other routes, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 keep the whole body up to maxBody, so one loop serves every version. gRPC client streams need this.

An answer sent before the body ends is followed by RST_STREAM NO_ERROR. A held stream's DATA still credits the connection window on arrival. A WINDOW_UPDATE that cannot fit in the output is retried later. The design is docs/http-one-handler.md §3.5. The guide gains "Reading a body in pieces on HTTP/2", and the http-server and http2 security records gain their streamed-body rows.

Part of #2125
Fixes #2124
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: decode request bodies under a decompression-bomb limit
entries.body:
`HttpHandler` now decodes a request body sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `x-gzip` or `deflate` (zlib-wrapped) before the route sees it. The decoded size is capped by the new `limits.maxDecoded` (one MiB by default; 0 turns decoding off). A body that would decode past the limit is answered 413, and a malformed one 400, without reaching the program. A small body that inflates to gigabytes costs under three times the limit in bytes written. `HttpRequest.decodedFrom` tells a route which coding was undone. `serve()` and the `HttpServer` façade do not decode yet.

Refs: docs/security/compress.md (COMP-18), docs/security/handler.md (HANDLER-16, HANDLER-17)
Tests: tests/link/net_handler_bomb

Part of #2123
Fixes #1931
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: streaming gRPC calls on the façade's HTTP/2 listeners (WP72 S6)
entries.body:
`GrpcServer` serves client-streaming, server-streaming and bidirectional calls on the façade's streaming request bodies, over h2c and TLS. `open` admits a streamed call, `next` reads its messages one at a time, `begin`, `send` and `finish` answer them, and `fail` ends a call with a status. A message over `maxMessage` is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a call's deadline, counted from when the server read the request's head, is DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; and a client's cancel ends the program's read. A message that spans DATA frames is copied into a buffer that grows as its bytes arrive. The buffer is capped at the declared length, and a body that ends short of it is refused before anything is allocated.

A Trailers-Only answer no longer keeps one of its connection's stream slots until the connection closes (GR-5). The interop job now calls each streaming kind with grpcurl on both listeners.

Fixes #2019
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: std/ panic ratchet, kept-panic rule and caller-proven spawn slots
entries.body:
`node tests/run.js std-panics` holds every std/ module's panic sites to a committed baseline, tests/std-panics.json, built from the compiler's own --emit-panics inventory. The check fails in four cases: a module's count rises, a new module arrives with sites, a count falls that the baseline does not record, or the kept and to-fix split no longer matches.

Each explicit panic(...) is either kept, listed by function with a reason, or counted as one to fix. A panic is kept only when it breaks a caller contract the function's doc states. Internal invariants, unreachable guards and real failures are counted to fix and assigned to the WP80-WP87 plans. docs/LANGUAGE.md states the rule under "Panics the standard library keeps".

A spawn's slot index (`spawn-slot`) and parallelMapInto's destination length (`parallel-length`) are now proven at the caller. That lets examples/tasks.ts and examples/histogram.ts build without --allow-panics. A guard that a later push, pop or rebinding undoes proves nothing, and the guard-then-mutate link tests pin that. NL2458 no longer refuses a call a second time for a site already inside the no-panic scope.

bench/std-threads.ts, std-json-typed.ts and std-cli-args.ts count the instructions of programs that drive std/threads, json-typed and cli-args.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: find the Threads page for multithreading searches and wrap code headings on phones
entries.body:
The docs search matches only a page's own words, and the Threads page never said "multithreading", "multicore" or "concurrency", so those searches found nothing. Its introduction now uses them in plain prose and points concurrency that mostly waits to async functions and the prefork server.

Headings with inline code broke mid-word on phones because Scalar lays a heading out as a flex row, making each text run and code span a shrinking item. Headings are now blocks that wrap between words, with the copy-link button placed after the last word in room kept by the heading's padding; the landing page's centred headings stay centred.

entries.title: match the panic ratchet's nish-cmp declarations to its release note
entries.body: The two DECLARED entries for the std-cli-args and std-json-typed instruction benches asked for "std/ panic ratchet", but changelog-gen capitalises a subject's first word, so the pending notes read "Std/ panic ratchet" and nish-cmp's case-sensitive lookup failed on main. They now ask for "panic ratchet".

entries.title: require a test for every bound a security record lists
entries.body:
Three WP72 stages (#2167, #2168, #2170) each listed a limit in a
docs/security record that no test pins (HTTPSRV-20, PB-6, GR-7), which
left that run's acceptance criterion 11 only partly met. A bound now
names the check that fails without it, or is recorded as untested.

entries.title: count std/net instructions and extend std/ panic-free for strict modules to DNS
entries.body:
std/net's DNS modules (dns-config, dns-message, dns-resolver, dns) now parse and build messages and read resolv.conf under guards the prover reads, so a strict module that resolves a host no longer inherits their implicit panic sites (484 before, 46 left, all explicit panics on caller arguments plus run-time-checked socket windows). dnsParseResolvConf with no nameserver line no longer panics when the caller's servers array is too short for the two fallback addresses.

Four std/net instruction benches (dns-message, quic-packet, tls-record, http2-frame) join the counted set in bench/instructions.json, so later WP82 stages are held to their instruction counts.

Refs: docs/security/dns.md
Tests: tests/link/net_dns_fallback_short
Fixes #2138

entries.title: make json-typed, cli-args, cli-flags and cli panic-free (WP80 S1)
entries.body:
std/json-typed, std/json, std/cli-args, std/cli-flags and std/cli no longer reach a panic site the caller cannot rule out: a failure the caller can cause is answered through checked Result twins, and an unreachable site carries a proof. std/threads keeps only caller-contract explicit panics, listed in tests/std-panics.json `kept`. api-cli, tasks and histogram build without --allow-panics; histogram-atomic keeps its opt-out for two src/ prover gaps (atomic element-method index sites and the type-only array-length check), recorded as follow-ups. New instruction-count bench programs cover HTTP/1 parse and write, router dispatch, ring push/pop, ThreadScope.spawn, json-typed decode and cli-args.

Fixes #2129
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net QUIC wire layer panic-free
entries.body:
The QUIC wire layer (quic-varint, quic-frame, quic-packet, quic-conn-cid, quic-datagram, quic-conn) now checks each window, length and counter before it indexes, slices or adds, and refuses with its sentinel instead of panicking. None of the six modules has a row left in tests/std-panics.json, so a new panic site fails the std-panics ratchet. The panic-free array helpers lose the boxed array-field layout, which moves HTTP3_SERVER_SLOT_BYTES to 111,240 bytes (+80).

Refs: docs/security/quic.md
Tests: tests/link/net_quic_packet, tests/link/net_quic_conn

Fixes #2141

entries.title: bring the refined WP72 plan to main
entries.body: The WP72 feature run refined its plan on a side branch: file lanes for each stage, the new S6a stage (streaming request bodies on the HTTP/2 listeners, #2124), and the build-ready wording for S5 and S6. This takes that copy to main and marks S5, S6a and S6 done: they merged as #2168, #2167 and #2170. The stage for #2172 is added by the next /feature #2008 run at sign-off.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: WP83 S1 — hashes, MACs and key derivation
entries.body:
* test(crypto): count HMAC, HKDF and an HS256 verify in the instruction gate

The instruction-count gate counted nine crypto kernels, none of which runs an
HMAC, an HKDF extract and expand or a JWT verify, so a change to
std/crypto/hmac.ts or std/crypto/hkdf.ts moved no counted program. The hash
family's existing `hmac-sha256` and `hkdf-sha256` kernels and
bench/jwt-verify's `verify` kernel are now counted too. Their baselines are
provisional ceilings until CI's runner prints its own figures.

Tests: node bench/run.mjs --instructions --only crypto

* test(crypto): set the HMAC, HKDF and HS256 verify instruction baselines to CI's counts

The three programs entered the gate with a 300M placeholder; this sets each to
the count CI's x86-64 runner printed for them on the previous head.

Measured: crypto-hmac-sha256 285,845,555; crypto-hkdf-sha256 296,149,871; crypto-jwt-verify 282,787,710 (valgrind-3.26.0 cachegrind, CI shard 9/9)

* fix(crypto): sha1 proves every index and hashes a message past 2^31 bytes

Sha1.digestInto answers false, writing nothing, for a range outside its
buffers instead of panicking, and sha1 walks its message with a number
offset, so under --number-mode f64 an array longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes is
hashed whole rather than refused. Every index and addition in the module
is proven in range.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_sha1, tests/link/crypto_sha1_long_f64

* fix(crypto): sha256 proves every index and hashes a message past 2^31 bytes

`sha256` and the new `Sha256.updateAll(data)` hash an array longer than
2^31 - 1 bytes whole, walking it a block at a time with a `number` offset,
where the one-shot used to panic. `Sha256.digestInto` answers `false` for a
window outside `out`, writing nothing, instead of panicking; a second
`digest` answers the same digest, and a copy of a finished hasher is
finished. `update` after `digest` still panics. Every index the compression
and padding read is now bounded by its loop's condition, so `--deny-panics`
callers see only those stated panics.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_sha256_long_f64, tests/link/crypto_sha256_digest_into_window, tests/link/crypto_sha256_copy_after_digest

* fix(crypto): sha512 proves every index and hashes a message past 2^31 bytes

`sha512` and `sha384` hash an array longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes whole
through the new `Sha512Engine.absorbAll(data)`, where they used to panic.
The engine writes its digest into the caller's array, and every index the
compression reads is bounded by its loop's condition.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_sha512_long_f64, tests/link/crypto_sha384_long_f64

* fix(crypto): hmac MACs a key or message past 2^31 bytes whole

`hmacSha256`, `hmacSha384`, `hmacSha512` and the keyed constructors MAC a
key or message longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes whole, through `Sha256.updateAll`
and `Sha512Engine.absorbAll`, where they used to panic. The pad, PBKDF2 and
keyed-copy loops prove their indices by their conditions. PBKDF2's dk
allocation keeps its length check: the prover cannot bound a length that
wide without a compiler change.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_hmac_sha256_long_f64, tests/link/crypto_hmac_sha256_long_key_f64, tests/link/crypto_hmac_sha384_long_f64

* fix(crypto): timingSafeEqualAt proves its indices

The window compare walks both windows with running positions its loop condition bounds, so no index check is left. The positions and lengths are public; the bytes are still read in constant time.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_ct, tests/link/crypto_ct_k1_copies

* fix(crypto): scram proves its indices

The client proof's XOR loop is bounded by its condition, so the SCRAM helpers keep no panic site.

Tests: tests/link/std_scram

* fix(crypto): hkdf proves its indices and extracts from IKM past 2^31 bytes

`hkdfExtractInto` MACs an input keying material longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes
whole, where it used to panic. Expand and Expand-Label build their info and
output with running positions their loop conditions bound, so the only
panics left are the ones the API states: a label, context, length or secret
outside HKDF-Expand-Label's bounds, and a hash length that is neither 32
nor 48.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_hkdf_scratch_long_f64, tests/link/crypto_hkdf_expand_label, tests/link/crypto_hkdf_k1_bounds

* fix(crypto): base64url proves its indices

The base64url and padded standard decoders and `base64StdPadEncodeInto`
read and write through running positions their conditions bound, in the
same constant-time arithmetic. The decoders' output allocations keep their
length check: the prover cannot bound a length that wide without a compiler
change.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_base64url, tests/link/crypto_base64url_groups, tests/link/std_base64_padded

* docs(crypto): record the panic sites of hashes, MACs and key derivation

The K1 record's addendum covers the one-shot hashes and MACs that now
hash an array past 2^31-1 bytes whole, Sha256.digestInto's false answer
for a bad window, and the three array-length sites kept for the prover.
The guide's sha256 row names updateAll and the false answer.

* chore(crypto): format the hashes, MACs and key derivation modules

* fix(crypto): keep base64urlDecode's text unkept for hashes, MACs and key derivation

The decode read its characters through a helper that took the text,
which escape analysis counts as keeping it, so a caller decoding an
arena string inside `using a = arena()` (examples/relay) was refused.
The reads are inline again; the bounds proof stays.

* chore(crypto): regenerate goldens, reference and panic counts for hashes, MACs and key derivation

* test(crypto): declare the nish-cmp moves of hashes, MACs and key derivation

ct.ll drops its index panics in every importer, three ct probes renumber
an attribute group, and the two sha1 probes call a digestInto the 0.44.0
seed's std returns void from, so the seed refuses them.

* docs(crypto): point the kept sites of hashes, MACs and key derivation at their current lines

* test(crypto): lower the hash, MAC and HS256 instruction ceilings to CI's counts

Every bench that reaches the hashes, MACs and key derivation this branch
changes now executes fewer instructions; each ceiling is set to the count CI's
x86-64 runner printed at baeb26ef.

Measured: crypto-sha256 123,979,154 (-1.641%); crypto-sha512 87,346,948 (-16.968%); crypto-hmac-sha256 278,589,272 (-2.539%); crypto-hkdf-sha256 274,453,587 (-7.326%); crypto-jwt-verify 271,034,368 (-4.156%) (valgrind-3.26.0 cachegrind, CI shard 9/9)

* docs(crypto): say a second Sha256 digest repeats the digest

A second digest or digestInto on a finished Sha256 now writes the same
32 bytes again instead of panicking, and a copy of a finished hasher is
finished too; the standard-library page says so.

* test(crypto): declare each program's hash, MAC and KDF module moves first

nish-cmp's declaredFor takes the first matching entry, so older file-only
declarations of sha1.ll, base64url.ll and scram.ll, and the HMAC digest
lists, covered this change's moves under other release notes. Each program
whose sha1, sha256, sha512, hmac, hkdf, base64url or scram module moves now
has a program-and-file entry at the head of DECLARED, listed from a run
against the 0.44.0 seed with those files undeclared: 2167 files in 455
programs.

* test(crypto): declare the hash, MAC and KDF moves in main's new net benches

bench/std-net-quic-packet and bench/std-net-tls-record, added by the DNS
panic-free change, reach hmac and hkdf, and std-net-tls-record declares the
Sha512 engine's new absorbAll and finish signatures in record.ll and its own
module; each gets its own program-and-file entry under this change's note.

* docs(crypto): state what a second digest does after WP83 S1

The K1 record's "Properties verified" row now says what the code does: a
Sha256 answers a second digest and copies a finished hasher, while the
SHA-512 engine and the HMACs still panic, HmacSha256 in its outer hasher's
update. K1-1's panic wording is marked superseded by the WP83 addendum, and
two Low findings are recorded open: HKDF's salt and PRK lengths saturating
under f64, and the zero digest of a wiped Sha256. The file-only ct.ll
nish-cmp entry is dropped, to be replaced by per-program entries.

* test(crypto): declare each program whose ct.ll moves under hashes, MACs and key derivation

The file-only ct.ll declaration would have covered a ct.ll move in any
program, now or later. It is replaced by one program and file entry for
each of the 428 corpus programs a nish-cmp run against the 0.44.0 seed
found writing a different ct.ll, in the head block with the other WP83 S1
moves.

* test(crypto): declare the hash, MAC and KDF moves in main's std-http1 bench

bench/std-http1.ts, added by the WP80 S1 change, reaches ct, hmac and hkdf,
and its record, tls and client modules declare the Sha512 engine's and
Sha256's new signatures; each moved module gets its own program-and-file
entry under this change's note.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: pin the date in net_handler_steps' warm arena rounds
entries.body: net_handler_steps measured arena growth across warm request rounds while the server's HTTP date was live. When the wall clock crossed a second boundary during those rounds, keepHead stopped reusing the cached response head and allocated a fresh one, so the arena check failed intermittently (+264 bytes) on unrelated PRs. The test now pins the server date for the warm rounds and unpins it afterwards, which makes the measurement independent of the clock.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: std/ panic-free for strict modules: std/sync, bytes, buffer-pool and prefork
entries.body:
std/sync's ring, region and pool, std/bytes, std/buffer-pool and std/net/prefork no longer panic on input a peer or caller controls. A ring a peer scribbled on answers RING_CORRUPT through checked twins, tryPreforkWith answers a refused config as an Err, and the remaining index sites carry proofs the prover reads, so the examples that used them drop --allow-panics.

Measured: std-ring 137385172 -> 129526568 instructions (valgrind 3.26, CI shard 9)
Tests: tests/link/net_prefork_checked, examples/prefork-jobs

Fixes #2130
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net TLS codec and record layer panic-free
entries.body:
The TLS handshake codec and record layer in std/net no longer reach a panic from peer input. Index and slice sites that a malformed or truncated record could drive out of range are now proven in range or guarded, and a bad length or an unexpected record ends the connection with a TLS alert instead of aborting the process. tests/std-panics.json records the lower panic and unproven-site counts, and the TLS security record lists the sites fixed and what is left.

Refs: docs/security/tls.md
Tests: tests/std-panics.json
Fixes #2139
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net TLS, fetch and outbound client side panic-free
entries.body:
This removes or proves the panic sites in the client side of std/net: tls, tls-tcp, fetch, http1-client-codec, outbound and upstream. The whole-file site count goes from 8075 to 7524.

It uses no nish:unsafe and no guards that make up a value. A real failure now returns its error code or Result, an unreachable site is proved, and the sites left are explicit caller-contract panics.

User-visible changes:
- http1-client-codec refuses a feed that would hold more than 2^30 unread bytes with the new HTTP1_E_MEMORY_LIMIT (18). It used to panic.
- outbound's filter and address helpers fail closed on out-of-range input.
- upstream's queue is a ring.

std/net TLS, fetch and outbound client side panic-free.

Refs: docs/MASTER_PLAN.md (WP82)
Tests: tests/std-panics.json, tests/link/net_http1_client*, tests/link/net_outbound*
Fixes #2140
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net QUIC engine and relay panic-free
entries.body:
The QUIC recovery, stream, connection and listener modules (std/net/quic-recovery.ts, quic-stream.ts, quic.ts, quic-listener.ts) no longer have implicit panic sites (index, overflow, divide, array-length, pop). A bad argument now gets a defined answer, such as a QUIC_ERROR_* code, false or a no-op, instead of a trap. Three explicit panics stay on purpose, as contract violations: QuicListener.handleWindow, QuicStreams.share and quicWorkerCheck.

A stream whose send pair the pool refuses, because the reserve is full, now keeps the pair, zeroed, until the next give-back. Before, the buffer was lost.

examples/relay builds against the new signatures. At boot, an unwritable --cert-out exits 1, and a renewal that cannot write the file keeps serving and prints the error.

Whole-file panic sites go from 7524 to 6986, and the explicit to-fix count from 109 to 106. HTTP3_SERVER_SLOT_BYTES moves by 368 bytes to 111608.

Changelog: the std/net QUIC engine

Refs: docs/security/quic.md
Tests: tests/link/net_quic_stream/pool.ts (sendKeptWhenFull)
Fixes #2142
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: WP81 S1 — postgres-carrier and postgres-async panic-free
entries.body:
The asynchronous PostgreSQL client and its carrier no longer panic on a short or malformed server message. Each such message now returns a Result error. The panic sites std-panics counts fell from 153 to 22 in std/net/postgres-carrier.ts and from 418 to 25 in std/net/postgres-async.ts. Every remaining site is kept with a reason.

New pg-codec and pg-carrier benches were pinned before any site changed. The pg-carrier bench runs a fixed four turns per round, so its instruction count does not depend on loopback timing.

Measured: on the same pg-carrier bench, this branch's postgres std counted 85,344,920 instructions against main's 85,676,614 (-0.39%, cachegrind)
Tests: node tests/run.js std-panics, node tests/run.js instructions, node tests/run.js net

Fixes #2135
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net HTTP/3 stack panic-free
entries.body:
Every panic site in std/net/http3.ts, http3-frame.ts, qpack.ts and http3-server.ts is either proven unreachable or removed, without nish:unsafe. Wire input that does not fit is refused with its protocol code (H3_FRAME_ERROR, H3_SETTINGS_ERROR, QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED, QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR, QPACK_DECODER_STREAM_ERROR) as the connection's CONNECTION_CLOSE. A site that can never be reached gets a guard the prover reads, and that guard fails the connection with H3_INTERNAL_ERROR, so no state is left half-built. Http3Connection.share no longer panics on pools of the wrong size and keeps its own pools instead. Panic sites across all modules fall from 6,462 to 6,019, and the to-fix count falls from 96 to 95. HTTP3_SERVER_SLOT_BYTES is now 111,488.

Refs: docs/security/http3.md
Tests: tests/link/net_http3_malformed

Fixes #2143
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the HTTP/1 wire layer panic-free (WP80 S3)
entries.body:
The HTTP/1 codec, the header fields, URL parsing and HTTP compression no longer panic. Real failures now come back as refusals, and the remaining sites are proven unreachable. The examples that needed --allow-panics only because of the wire layer no longer need it.

Fixes #2131
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: match nish-cmp's changelog words as the generator renders them
entries.body: nish-cmp excuses a declared IR difference only when the declaration's words appear in CHANGELOG.md or the pending release notes. Those words are copied from the squash subject, which a conventional commit keeps lower case, but scripts/changelog-gen.mjs raises a title's first letter when it renders the notes. A declaration quoting a subject's opening was therefore never found, and main's nish-cmp jobs failed on #2193's "make the HTTP/1 wire layer panic-free". The lookup now also accepts the words with the first letter raised, exactly as renderEntry does, and its self-check covers both the lower-case match and the cases that must still miss.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the std/net HTTP/2 stack and HPACK panic-free
entries.body:
std/net/http2.ts, http2-frame.ts, http2-cleartext.ts, http2-tls.ts and hpack.ts now answer malformed peer input with a Result or an error code instead of a panic. HPACK table, integer, string and Huffman decoding return HPACK_ERR_* codes. Input feed, header-block gather and compaction copy with tryCopyBytes. The frame writers share one length clamp. http2IsPreface accepts only the whole 24-byte preface. Unproven panic sites in these modules go from 351 to 29, the rest being kept-list caller contracts recorded in the security records.

Refs: docs/security/http2.md, docs/security/http2-cleartext.md
Tests: tests/link/net_hpack_malformed, tests/link/net_http2

Fixes #2144
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make the HTTP/1 server panic-free (WP80 S4)
entries.body:
Clears the panic sites of std/net/http1-server.ts (166 to 6) and std/net/http-server.ts (451 to 49) without nish:unsafe or invented values. A real failure now answers with a refusal (null, false, H1_CLOSED, 503 or 431), and an unreachable site is guarded or proved. A head whose spans do not fit the request record is refused with 431 rather than truncated. The module and its importers compile under --number-mode f64.

Fixes #2132
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make handler, serve and static panic-free for http-app (WP80 S5)
entries.body:
Clears the panic sites std/net/handler.ts, serve.ts and static.ts reach from examples/http-app. A real failure is refused rather than panicking: StaticFiles decodes the path with tryPercentDecode, so a bad escape answers 404. The http-app header and its guide markers now list only the sites http-app still reaches, chiefly the Http1Connection constructor's capacity check. The router rework is held back as a separate decision (+4.3% std-router).

Fixes #2133
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: WP83 S2 — ciphers, curves, signatures and password hashing
entries.body:
* fix(runtime): clear the x25519 and ed25519 panic sites

The bit counters in the field's byte packing use the file's wrapping u64
helpers, the precomputed table has a named constant length, the table's
blends and stores walk with each index tested against its array, and the
point decoder packs into fixed 32-byte buffers. ed25519 keeps its two
recorded panics in sign and verify.

* fix(runtime): keep x25519's field packing as its constant-time copy has it

The wrapping-helper edit to the bit counters moved f25519DecodeInto and
f25519EncodeInto away from the copies tests/cases/ct_asm_x25519.ts holds
them to, so they stay as main has them; ed25519's decoder checks the
length of the two encodings it indexes instead.

* fix(runtime): clear chacha20poly1305 panic sites outside its constant-time copy

Reads each window's last byte first so one bounds check covers the rest,
sums the tag offset and counter in unsigned arithmetic, and allocates the
Poly1305 tag with a literal length the prover reads.

* fix(runtime): clear AES-GCM panic sites outside its constant-time copy

Reads and stores each block's highest index first so one bounds check
covers the rest, sizes the key schedule and counter buffers with literal
lengths the prover reads, and rounds block counts up with shifts that
cannot overflow.

* fix(runtime): clear bcrypt panic sites outside its generated round bodies

Walks the salt, key and state copies with cursors the loop bounds,
sizes the encoding and batch buffers with literal lengths, and keeps the
key schedule's position masked so it needs no check; the secret S-box
reads and the generated round bodies are unchanged.

* test(runtime): lower the std-panics ratchet for the cipher, curve and bcrypt modules

Regenerates the checked goldens the std/crypto edits move and lowers
tests/std-panics.json for aes, chacha20poly1305, ed25519, bcrypt and
bcrypt-batch.

Tests: std-panics

* fix(runtime): refuse an oversized Ed25519 message and wrap the bcrypt batcher's ticket

ed25519Sign now answers null and ed25519Verify false for a message longer
than 2^31 - 1 bytes, where both panicked; under --number-mode f64 the length
is attacker-chosen. BcryptBatcher's ticket counter wrapped to a panic at its
2^31st request (BCRYPT-12, Medium); it now wraps to 0. Also formats the AES
and bcrypt changes and drops two batch-state constants they left unused.

Tests: tests/link/thread_bcrypt_batcher, tests/link/crypto_ed25519_f64

* test(runtime): prove or refuse the panic sites in ciphers, curves, signatures and password hashing

Declares the one nish-cmp row this stage moves: thread_bcrypt_batcher now
drives the batcher's ticket past 2^31 - 1, and the seed numbers an attribute
group in its main.ll differently from the candidate.

* perf(runtime): test the Ed25519 table blend's lengths once per limb walk

The constant-time table select blended each limb under four bounds tests;
it now tests the destination once and the source once per limb, which the
bounds prover still discharges, so crypto-ed25519-sign stays below its
instruction baseline.

* fix(runtime): say that BcryptBatcher tickets wrap, and test the wrapped answer

BcryptBatcher's verify and hash now document that tickets count up from 0
and wrap to 0 after 2^31 - 1, and the password-hashing guide says to match
answers by ticket rather than assume a later request has a larger one. The
batcher test checks that the wrapped request's answer carries ticket 0. The
ed25519 blend comment now says which lengths are tested once and which per
limb.

Tests: tests/link/thread_bcrypt_batcher

* fix(runtime): prove or refuse the AES schedule, GHASH length and bcrypt batch salt guards

aesScheduleInto no longer returns early on a round count other than 10
or 14: it is an i32 only because the kernel takes one, and both callers
pass one of the two. ghashLengths takes H's two words from the entry
point, which refuses a key whose hash key is not two words long, so it
no longer returns on a short array. BcryptBatcher keeps each request's
salt as its own array instead of slicing a shared buffer at 16 times
the request's index, so no index past the buffer reads a zero salt; a
hash request without a 16-byte salt is answered with bcrypt's error.

* fix(runtime): read no lane of a bcrypt batch past its end

bcryptBatchLane read list[0] for a lane past the batch's end and then
passed that lane as null; it now answers null without reading list, and
an empty batch is answered with an error instead of a panic.

* test(runtime): declare each corpus file the cipher stage moves

nish-cmp matched the IR moves of aes.ll, chacha20poly1305.ll, ed25519.ll,
bcrypt.ll, bcrypt-batch.ll and thread_bcrypt_batcher's main.h against older
entries, because a program's first matching entry wins. Each now has a narrow
STD_CIPHER_PANIC_FREE entry per program, placed ahead of the older ones:
829 entries, found by compiling the 319 corpus programs that reach the five
modules against main's and this branch's std/ with one compiler, with and
without sidecars.

Tests: tests/nish-cmp.js

* test(runtime): declare the cipher moves of main's new TLS and QUIC benches

bench/std-net-quic-packet.ts and bench/std-net-tls-record.ts came in with
main and write aes.ll and chacha20poly1305.ll, which this stage moves; each
joins those two STD_CIPHER_PANIC_FREE lists.

Tests: tests/nish-cmp.js

* test(self): lower std-panics after merging main

* test(self): declare the cipher moves in main's new HTTP/1 bench

bench/std-http1.ts, new on main, links aes.ts, chacha20poly1305.ts and
ed25519.ts, so its copies of those modules move with this stage's index
proofs; the stage's narrow entries now name it.

std/README.md's Ed25519 row still said both panic on such a message; the
stage's code refuses it instead (ECC-5).

entries.title: WP83 S3 — P-256, P-384, RSA and JWT
entries.body:
Clear the unproven panic sites in std/crypto/p256.ts, p384.ts, rsa.ts and jwt.ts: each made-up-value guard becomes a refusal where failure is real or a proof the prover discharges. Only p256SignSha256Into's two window panics and JwtVerifier's constructor stay on the kept list. Every Secret wipe and constant-time property is kept.

Fixes #2149
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make std/net/router.ts panic-free (WP80 S6)
entries.body:
std/net/router.ts now proves every index, array length and arithmetic site it reaches: the constructor clamps maxSegments and maxParams to routerLimit's 256, and growStatic stops doubling past 2^30. Only its six kept explicit panics remain, and tests/std-panics.json drops from 3732 to 3602.

The std-router bench rises 4.32% (155,580,314 to 162,304,316 instructions, CI's printed figure), an exception accepted on #2204.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: bound the DNS query deadline and record what WP82 S9 leaves (WP82 S9)
entries.body:
* fix(runtime): bound the DNS query deadline and record what WP82 S9 leaves (WP82 S9)

The resolver's query deadline no longer overflows: dnsResolverDeadline adds
the timeout only to a clock within 2^62 ns of 0, gives a later clock a
deadline no clock reaches and an earlier one itself, so the last overflow
in std/net/dns-resolver.ts is gone. tlsHeldWindow's panic is kept as the
caller contract tlsDeriveSecretHeld and tlsFinishedVerifyDataHeld document.

The io-exit sites S1-S7 left are all crypto.getRandomValues, and the slice
sites are the window checks of the netRead, netWrite, udpSendTo and
udpRecvFrom builtins: neither can be cleared from std, so the plan's S9
stage records them as compiler work, examples/http-get-json.ts keeps its
opt-out with a header naming each site, and the guide's allow-panics
markers now name the sites that remain instead of the TLS record layer.

Tests: tests/std-panics.json, tests/link/std_dns_caps

* test(self): rewrite the std panic counts after syncing main
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: WP83 S4 — X.509 and the PKI
entries.body:
The unproven panic sites in nish/crypto/x509, pki, pki-roots and
x509-random are cleared: a malformed certificate, chain, host name or
PEM bundle now gets the error value its function documents, never a
panic. x509DerText answers null rather than an empty name, and its
callers refuse it. The std-panics ratchet drops from 3601 to 3410.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make WebTransport, WebSocket, gRPC and OIDC panic-free (WP82 S8)
entries.body:
* fix(runtime): make WebSocket framing and handshake panic-free

websocketWriteFrame and websocketFrame answer WS_REFUSED and null for a
payload window outside the buffer instead of panicking, and the decoder
returns a close code where its buffers would not hold a frame. Only the
two documented panics stay: websocketIsUtf8 and WsDecoder.feed on a
window outside their own buffer.

Tests: tests/link/net_websocket_frame_window, tests/link/net_websocket_write_window

* fix(runtime): make OIDC key-set parsing and cache lifetimes panic-free

The Cache-Control reader saturates an i32 age and slices with substring,
the key lookups read local arrays, and the token buffer is sized through a
helper that refuses a negative length. What stays is the caller's clock in
i64 and the two String.fromBytes reads.

* style(runtime): format the WebSocket module

* fix(runtime): make gRPC framing and streaming reads panic-free

Each request index's call is one GrpcCall object found through a guarded
lookup, so the per-call fields need no index of their own. Prefixes are
read by one bounds-checked helper, split messages copy with tryCopyBytes
and answer INTERNAL when the copy cannot be made, status values and the
length prefix are built fresh, and grpc-timeout is parsed in i32 and
scaled in f64. The caller-contract panics stay.

* fix(runtime): keep WebTransport's sessions and streams in objects

Each session's state and each stream slot's state now live in one object,
reached through a guarded lookup, so the parallel per-session arrays no
longer need an unproven index at every touch. A CLOSE capsule reads into
its session's own reason buffer, and a capsule or datagram past its buffer
answers H3_TOO_LARGE instead of panicking. The code mappings and the
waiting-stream hash are worked in f64, which holds their values exactly.

* test(runtime): lower the std panic counts for the realtime net modules

WsAcceptKey allocates its fixed 60-byte input directly: the growing
allocator it called made the prover drop the span bound in the HTTP/1
server's acceptWebSocket, which reads spans after the call.

* test(self): regenerate the checked goldens for the realtime net modules

* docs(runtime): regenerate the WebSocket and WebTransport reference pages

* fix(runtime): make WebTransport, WebSocket, gRPC and OIDC panic-free (WP82 S8)

The WebSocket frame writers answer a window outside the payload, a
negative length or a mask that is not 4 bytes with WS_REFUSED, and a
buffer too small for the frame with WS_NO_ROOM, so a program calling them
builds under the no-panic default. WebTransport, gRPC and OIDC guard or
prove every index they touch on a peer's bytes. The panics left are the
program's own mistakes the modules keep on purpose and clock arithmetic
that overflows only for a reading near 2^63.

Refs: docs/security/webtransport.md, docs/security/grpc.md, docs/security/oidc.md, docs/security/http1-codec.md
Tests: tests/link/net_websocket_malformed_strict, tests/std-panics.json

* perf(runtime): allocate realtime net buffers once and clear S8's performance warnings

websocketBytes, wtBytes, wtI32s, wtI64s and grpcBytes allocate a non-negative
length in one array instead of pushing past 64 KiB byte by byte. oidcLifetime's
last substring is bounded by a test the prover reads, WebTransportSession
declares its fields widest first, and the per-session arrays on WebTransport
are documented as read-only copies of each session's state.

* fix(runtime): keep the realtime net buffers' proven allocation

Return websocketBytes, wtBytes, wtI32s, wtI64s and grpcBytes to the u16-sized
allocation the prover discharges; a u32 length is an unproven array-length site.

* test(self): regenerate the relay golden and WebTransport reference

The WebTransportSession field order and the read-only notes on the per-session
arrays move the checked golden and the generated reference.

* test(self): rewrite the std panic counts after syncing main
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse a new inline function program in the test harnesses
entries.body:
The arrow-corpus check read only tests/**/*.ts, so a Nish program written as
a string literal in tests/run.js or another harness could add a top-level
`function` definition and pass CI; #1743 and #1748 converted such programs by
hand after #1722. scripts/inline-functions.mjs now reads every tracked
tests/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs} file with TypeScript's parser and fails on a string or
template literal whose text opens a `function` definition, naming the file,
the line and the fix. A literal that must keep the spelling (a host module,
arrowify's own unit cases, a syntax-error source, the interop's .d.ts text)
carries a `// nish-function: <reason>` comment at the literal or its
statement; a marker with no reason, one that covers nothing, and a file the
parser cannot read fail too. The arrow-corpus section runs it and proves it
on a scratch repository: a probe program fails, removing it passes.

The five inline programs added since #1748 (the package-link library and four
c-import mains) are spelled as const arrows.
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: WP81 S2 — postgres panic-free
entries.body:
std/net/postgres.ts (the blocking client, its pool, batcher and batch clock)
goes from 556 unproven panic sites to 99: every overflow and divide site is
proved, and index sites fall from 139 to 16. Malformed or short server frames
(a truncated length, a column count past the frame, a DataRow cut short) now
fail the connection as a framing error instead of panicking. pgFind and
pgPutDecimal no longer hold an explicit panic. The 16 index sites left are the
caller-c column accessors, whose column index is the caller's contract. The
output writer's putByte and putI32 write straight into the buffer when there is
room, which more than pays for the new guards.

Measured: pg-codec 176,324,257 instructions (pin 186,746,194, -5.6%); pg-carrier 85,307,674 (pin 85,797,412, -0.6%); CI cachegrind, tolerance +0.1%
Refs: docs/security/postgres.md
Tests: tests/link/std_postgres, tests/std-panics.json

Fixes #2136
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: make checksum, zlib and gzip panic-free
entries.body:
std/compress/checksum.ts, zlib.ts and gzip.ts now hold no unproven panic site. A corrupt, truncated or oversized stream answers an error code, and the bit and length arithmetic carries proofs the compiler accepts. Crc32.update no longer checks its own tables. A GzipWriter used after finish answers the new GZIP_ERR_FINISHED code from write, flush and finish, where it used to panic. GzipWriter.bound and gzipFixedBound answer DEFLATE_NO_ROOM past their largest input, where the sum used to overflow. The remaining explicit panics are caller misuse: a window outside its array, a negative limit, and GzipReader.commit and read outside their ranges.

Four instruction-count programs now drive the std/compress code the panic ratchet counts: std-compress-deflate, -inflate, -checksum and -gzip. Their counts were baselined on CI's runner before any site changed.

Measured: instructions (cachegrind, CI runner): std-compress-checksum 109,018,226 → 106,368,115 (-2.43%), std-compress-gzip 189,505,675 → 189,410,010 (-0.05%), deflate and inflate unchanged at baseline
Tests: tests/link/std_compress_gzip_errors
Verified: pr-adversary 1 round, CI green

Fixes #2152
